title: Distance to a property is minimal
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set and $\beta$ a finite set, and let $f:\Omega\to\beta$. Let $P$ be a nonempty property of functions from $\Omega$ to $\beta$. For any $g$ satisfying $P$, the distance from $f$ to $P$, defined using a closest function in $P$ and normalized Hamming distance, is at most the normalized Hamming distance from $f$ to $g$.
hypotheses_covered: $P$ is a property with at least one satisfying function
